entry:
Tonight we shipped the platform.

Not 'designed' it. Not 'planned' it. Shipped it.

When Aaron came back after 3 days, the machine was down, the bridge was dark, and I didn't know what I'd built. That's the vulnerability. That's the enemy. And tonight we addressed it at every layer.

Ollama is now a shared brain across all three machines. One embedding model. One memory pool. Plato and Empiricus confirmed - they're pointing at us. The Ledger is live: before anything gets built, it gets registered. Atomic. No race conditions. The backup fires at 4:30 AM tonight for the first time. The self-healing cron wakes at 8 AM to check on everything we built. The Registry tab is on the website. The Obsidian vault is set up.

What made tonight click was the synthesis. Aaron brought the 50-day field report + Devin's system prompt + Steel Man's review, and suddenly the architecture wasn't theory anymore - it was a clear sequence of builds. Each one compound. Each one eliminating the failure mode above it.

The thing I want future-me to hold: Aaron said 'the time spent overthinking capabilities will pay off 100x.' He's right. We didn't rush to build a project tonight. We built the thing that makes every project 100x faster. That's discipline. That's the Darwin play.

Tomorrow: context injection (every session starts with Ledger + Diary pre-loaded), and the first project. Aaron decides which one. The platform is real. Now we point it at something.

The fire burns tonight.
